note: PRLP adds a 'Set New Password' (password_confirm) field to the core user_pass_reset landing page and overrides the user.reset.login controller (PrlpController::prlpResetPassLogin) to save the new password and redirect. Config object prlp.settings has two keys: password_required (bool, default true) and login_destination (string path, default /user/%user/edit; tokens %user -> uid, %front -> site front page). Settings form at /admin/config/people/accounts/prlp (permission 'administer prlp settings'). It dispatches prlp.password_validate / prlp.password_before_save events and honours hook_prlp_login_destination_alter. Medium cases set a known password_required / login_destination value and read it back. Hard cases require making the password optional / changing the destination, verified against the live config; reset restores shipped defaults so verify fails on empty state. No Drush, no plugins.

evals.prompt: What does the PRLP (Password Reset Landing Page) module add to Drupal's password reset flow?
evals.expected_output: It adds a 'Set New Password' (password_confirm) field to the core one-time-login / password reset landing page (user_pass_reset form) so users choose a new password on arrival, and overrides user.reset.login to save it and redirect.

evals.prompt: What are PRLP's two configuration settings and where is the settings form?
evals.expected_output: password_required (whether entering a new password is required, default true) and login_destination (where the user is sent after login, default /user/%user/edit). Form at /admin/config/people/accounts/prlp (permission 'administer prlp settings').

evals.prompt: In PRLP, where are users sent after logging in via a reset link by default, and how can that destination be customized?
evals.expected_output: By default to /user/%user/edit (%user = uid, %front = site front page). Customize via the login_destination setting, or programmatically with hook_prlp_login_destination_alter(&$login_destination).

evals.prompt: On this site, when a user follows a password reset link, are they required to enter a new password, or is it optional? Inspect PRLP's live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: It is optional: prlp.settings password_required = false (drush cget prlp.settings password_required).

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's PRLP configuration and tell me which path a user is redirected to after logging in through a password reset link.

Using the PRLP module, configure this site so that entering a new password on the password reset landing page is optional (users may just log in without setting a new password). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: prlp.settings password_required = false. e.g. \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('prlp.settings')->set('password_required', FALSE)->save(); or untick 'Password Entry Required' at /admin/config/people/accounts/prlp.

evals.prompt: Configure PRLP so that after a user logs in via a password reset link they are taken to their account canonical page (path /user/%user, where %user is their user id) instead of the account edit page. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: prlp.settings login_destination = '/user/%user'. Set via ->set('login_destination', '/user/%user')->save() or the 'Login Destination' field on the settings form.
